title: Customers and their active 2026 policies (Oracle outer join)
businessPurpose: Underwriting wants every customer with the number and premium of policies that started in 2026 and are active, including customers with none, for the renewal outreach list.

invariants.name: policy count is conserved
invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM policies WHERE status_code = 'AC' AND effective_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'

invariants.name: premium is conserved
invariants.sql: SELECT COALESCE(sum(annual_premium), 0) FROM policies WHERE status_code = 'AC' AND effective_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'

candidates.why: Both Oracle (+) predicates are in the LEFT JOIN's ON clause.
Executable and plausible, but drops customers 5, 6 and 7. The headline silent failure.
COUNT(*) instead of COUNT(p.policy_id) reports a policy for customers who have none.
Half-moved predicate: customers whose only policy is lapsed are dropped.
The right rows in the wrong order: ORDER BY customer_id DESC where the legacy query sorts ascending. Same multiset of rows, so only the row-order check sees it.
Right on every primary row by construction: customers above id 4 are forced to zero. Only data it has not seen shows it is wrong.
